title: Self-Esteem, Shame & the Inner Critic
description: Explore confidence in a skill versus global worth through dialogue, evidence and psychological reasoning.

lessons.title: One mark becomes a verdict
lessons.teach: Follow the conversation one message at a time. Notice what the behaviour might be achieving before you decide why it happened. About five minutes.
lessons.objective: Distinguish observable evidence from a tentative explanation of confidence in a skill versus global worth.

nodes.title: What might be happening?
nodes.body:
Confidence in a skill concerns the likelihood of doing a task well. Global self-worth concerns how someone evaluates themselves as a person. When the two become fused, corrective feedback can feel like an identity threat, making the precise improvement harder to act on.

The assessment may reveal a genuine weakness. Accurate feedback and a less global judgement can coexist.

nodes.explanation: The trigger is hal receives an unsuccessful assessment result. Its possible meaning is he interprets one weak section as evidence he does not belong in the profession. The protective behaviour may contribute to a longer-term cost: the judgement may discourage the very learning needed to improve.
nodes.counterexample: The assessment may reveal a genuine weakness. Accurate feedback and a less global judgement can coexist.

nodes.title: One distinction to keep
nodes.prompt: Fill the missing word: An explanation of what a behaviour might achieve is a working ______, not a proven fact.
nodes.explanation: A hypothesis is an explanation that can be revised when observations fail to support it. This keeps psychological reasoning useful rather than turning it into confident mind-reading.
